kcet|Chemistry|2012|27||0|0.s:
Free energy and the equilibrium constant are linked by
ΔG° = −2.303 RT log K
K = 0.008, which is less than 1, so log K is negative and ΔG° will come out positive.
log K = log(8 × 10⁻³) = log 8 − 3 = 0.903 − 3 = −2.097
Now substitute, with R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ and T = 298 K:
ΔG° = −2.303 × 8.314 × 298 × (−2.097)
2.303 × 8.314 × 298 = 5705
ΔG° = −5705 × (−2.097) = +11963 J
= +11.96 kJ
The sign is the thing to watch: K < 1 means the reaction does not favour products, so ΔG°
must be positive ✓
∴ +11.96 kJ.

kcet|Chemistry|2012|28||0|0.s:
Froth flotation separates a sulphide ore from its gangue using the difference in wettability.
Potassium ethyl xanthate is a **collector**. Its molecule has two ends: a sulphur-containing head
that binds firmly to the sulphide mineral surface, and a hydrocarbon tail that points outwards.
That hydrocarbon tail is non-polar, so the coated particle becomes **water repellent**
(hydrophobic). It is no longer wetted by the water, attaches instead to the air bubbles blown
through the pulp, and rises with the froth to be skimmed off.
The gangue — silicates and oxides — stays wetted and sinks.
If the collector made the ore *attracted* to water, as option (1) says, the ore would sink with
the gangue and the separation would fail entirely.
Pine oil acts as the frother, stabilising the bubbles, a separate job.
∴ to make the ore water repellent.

kcet|Chemistry|2012|29||0|0.s:
Electronegativity increases **across** a period and decreases **down** a group.
Place the four elements:
N, O and F are all in period 2, in that order from left to right.
P is directly below N, in period 3.
Across period 2, left to right: N < O < F, so F is the highest of all — indeed the highest of any
element, at 4.0.
Down group 15: N is above P, so N > P.
Pauling values: F 4.0, O 3.5, N 3.0, P 2.1
Putting them in decreasing order:
F > O > N > P
The one to watch is P, which is the lowest despite nitrogen being its group partner — going
down a group the atom is larger and holds bonding electrons less tightly.
∴ F > O > N > P.

kcet|Chemistry|2012|30||0|0:
Buna rubbers take their name from their ingredients: **Bu** from butadiene and **Na** from
natrium, the Latin for sodium.
Sodium metal was the catalyst used in the original polymerisation of buta-1,3-diene, initiating
the chain by adding an electron to the diene and starting the anionic polymerisation.
So the s-block element in question is sodium, and its name is built into the product's name —
which is the clue the question is relying on.
The other options are all s-block metals but none is used here: magnesium and calcium appear
in Grignard and carbide chemistry, barium in sulphate and peroxide chemistry.
Buna-S adds styrene as the comonomer, Buna-N adds acrylonitrile, but the sodium is common
to both.
∴ sodium.
kcet|Chemistry|2012|31||0|0:
Find the property that covalent compounds do **not** have.
(1) True — covalent molecules are held to one another only by weak van der Waals forces or
hydrogen bonds, so little energy is needed to separate them and melting points are low.
(3) True — 'like dissolves like'. Non-polar covalent compounds dissolve in non-polar solvents
such as benzene, not in polar ones such as water.
(4) True — a covalent bond forms when the electronegativity difference is small, so neither
atom can take the electrons outright and they are shared instead.
(2) False — covalent compounds have a very **definite** geometry. The bond is formed by the
overlap of specific orbitals pointing in specific directions, so it is directional, and the shape
follows from VSEPR: methane is tetrahedral, water bent, ammonia pyramidal, always with the
same angles.
It is **ionic** bonding that is non-directional, because the electrostatic field of an ion is the
same in every direction.
∴ 'no definite geometry' is not a characteristic of a covalent compound.

kcet|Chemistry|2012|32||0|0.s:
Balance the redox reaction first to get the mole ratio.
Oxidation: C₂O₄²⁻ ⇒ 2CO₂ + 2e⁻ (2 electrons each)
Reduction: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ ⇒ Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O (5 electrons each)
For the electrons to cancel, 5 oxalates are needed for every 2 permanganates:
5C₂O₄²⁻ + 2MnO₄⁻ + 16H⁺ ⇒ 2Mn²⁺ + 10CO₂ + 8H₂O
moles of KMnO₄ = 0.020 L × 0.025 mol L⁻¹ = 5 × 10⁻⁴ mol
moles of oxalic acid = (5/2) × 5 × 10⁻⁴ = 1.25 × 10⁻³ mol
Volume of 0.1 M oxalic acid:
V = 1.25 × 10⁻³ / 0.1 = 0.0125 L = 12.5 ml
Using a 1 : 1 ratio instead would give 5 ml, and inverting the ratio gives 2 ml — the
stoichiometry is where this question is won or lost.
∴ 12.5 ml.

kcet|Chemistry|2012|33||0|0.s:
A ligand bonds to the central metal through a **coordinate** bond, and in a coordinate bond one
partner supplies both of the shared electrons.
The metal ion is electron deficient — it has vacant orbitals and a positive charge — so it is the
acceptor. The ligand must therefore be the **donor** of the electron pair.
On the Lewis definition, an electron-pair donor is a **base**.
So every ligand is a Lewis base: NH₃ donates the lone pair on nitrogen, H₂O through oxygen,
Cl⁻ and CN⁻ through their lone pairs.
It follows that the metal ion acting as the acceptor is the Lewis **acid**, and the complex is
simply a Lewis acid–base adduct.
Note this is independent of Brønsted acidity — a ligand need have no hydrogen at all.
∴ a ligand is a Lewis base.

kcet|Chemistry|2012|34||0|0.s:
Use Raoult's law for the liquid phase and Dalton's law for the vapour.
Let p°A = p and p°B = 2p, since their ratio is 1 : 2.
The liquid has A and B in the ratio 1 : 2, so
xA = 1/3 and xB = 2/3
Partial pressures:
pA = xA·p°A = (1/3)(p) = p/3
pB = xB·p°B = (2/3)(2p) = 4p/3
Total pressure = p/3 + 4p/3 = 5p/3
The mole fraction in the **vapour** is the partial pressure over the total:
yA = pA / ptotal = (p/3) / (5p/3) = 1/5 = 0.2
Notice the vapour is poorer in A (0.2) than the liquid was (0.33), because A is the less volatile
component — the vapour is always richer in the more volatile one.
∴ 0.2.

kcet|Chemistry|2012|35||0|0:
Test each statement against the two laws of thermodynamics.
The **first law** is conservation of energy: energy can be converted from one form to another
but cannot be created or destroyed. Applied to the universe as a whole, which exchanges
nothing with anything outside itself, the total energy is therefore **constant** ✓
That makes (4) true and (3) false.
The **second law** says the entropy of an isolated system increases for any spontaneous
process. Every real process in the universe is irreversible, so the total entropy is continuously
**increasing**.
That makes (1) false, since entropy is not constant, and (2) false, since it increases rather
than decreases.
Clausius summarised both together: the energy of the universe is constant; the entropy of the
universe tends to a maximum.
∴ the total energy of the universe remains constant.
kcet|Chemistry|2012|36||0|0:
Work in milliequivalents, since normalities are given.
meq of NaOH = volume × normality = 5 × 0.4 = 2
meq of HCl = 20 × 0.1 = 2
The two are **exactly equal**, so the strong acid and the strong base neutralise each other
completely:
NaOH + HCl ⇒ NaCl + H₂O
Nothing is left over — no excess H⁺ and no excess OH⁻.
What remains is sodium chloride, the salt of a strong acid and a strong base. Neither ion
hydrolyses: Na⁺ is too weak an acid and Cl⁻ too weak a base to affect the water.
So the solution is simply neutral, with [H⁺] = 10⁻⁷ M.
∴ pH = 7.
kcet|Chemistry|2012|37||0|0:
The starting solution is 20 ml of 0.1 N HCl, so [H⁺] = 0.1 M and pH = 1.
The pH is unchanged only if [H⁺] stays at 0.1 M.
(1) Adding 1 ml of 1 N HCl adds 1 meq to the existing 2 meq, giving 3 meq in 21 ml, a
normality of 0.143 — more concentrated, so the pH falls.
(2) Adding 20 ml of water halves the concentration to 0.05 N, so the pH rises to about 1.3.
(3) Adding 1 ml of 0.1 N NaOH neutralises 0.1 meq, leaving 1.9 meq in 21 ml — the pH rises.
(4) HCl of pH 1 **is** 0.1 N HCl. Adding 500 ml of a solution to 20 ml of the identical solution
changes the volume but not the concentration, so [H⁺] stays at 0.1 M throughout.
That is the key realisation: pH is an intensive property and does not depend on how much you
have, only on how concentrated it is.
∴ adding 500 ml of HCl of pH = 1.
